assessment: The source provides a quantitative study of wave-packet dynamics across the Anderson transition on small-world graphs, with two distinct regimes (localized and delocalized) that share controls (K, t) and readouts (Pi(0,t), tau_loc, tau_ergo). The localized regime yields a finite-time scaling law with exponent nu_loc ~ 1.06, and the delocalized regime yields an ergodic time scaling with exponent nu = 0.5. These form a coherent quantitative cluster suitable for authoring.

paper_scope: The paper studies the critical dynamics of the Anderson transition on small-world graphs using a unitary kicked model (UASW). It focuses on wave-packet dynamics, return probability, localization times, and ergodic time scaling across localized, critical, and delocalized regimes.
